newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli opposition leader to meet King Hussein.
newsitem.headline: Israeli opposition leader to meet King Hussein.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak will meet Jordan's King Hussein on Monday, Barak's spokeswoman said on Sunday.
"He will leave Israel at 4:30 p.m. (1330 GMT) for the meeting," Merav Parsi-Zadok told Reuters.
Last week, as expected, Barak won a landslide victory in the race for leader of Israel's main opposition Labour party.

He vowed to press for early elections to oust Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Netanyahu defeated Labour leader Shimon Peres in elections a year ago. The next Israeli general election is set for 2000.

The Labour-led government, guided by the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace, had struck an interim peace deal with the Palestinians and signed a peace treaty with Jordan during its tenure.
Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace but has said he would uphold deals signed by the prior government.
In March, King Hussein wrote a letter to Netanyahu saying he did not trust him and warning of an impending explosion of the Middle East peace process.
Days later, on March 18, Netanyahu sent bulldozers to begin construction of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, plunging peacemaking with the Palestinians into deep crisis.
